title: Eliminating Parameters in Linear Trajectories
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Eliminate the parameter t from the parametric equations x = 2t - 1, y = 3t + 4 (-inf < t < inf) to find a Cartesian equation of the curve in slope-intercept form.

steps.title: Solve for Parameter t in Terms of x
steps.explanation: Isolate the parameter t in the x-equation.
steps.why: Algebraic substitution allows elimination of an intermediate parameter variable.

steps.title: Substitute t into the y-Equation
steps.explanation: Replace t with (x + 1)/2 in the expression for y and combine like terms.
steps.why: Pointwise evaluation yields the direct Cartesian relationship between y and x.

steps.title: Identify Geometric Features
steps.explanation: The curve is a straight line with slope m = dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) = 3/2 and y-intercept 11/2.
steps.why: Linear parametric equations x = x0 + at, y = y0 + bt trace a straight line with slope b/a.
